reviews.review: Really fun! I played the whole game in one sitting. The outcome was interesting. All in all 4/5!

So, I can say with certainty that, after my first playthrough, I intend to play Simulacra several times more. The flow of the narrative it's really good and it doesn't sink at all so it keeps you interested and focused the whole time. Thanks to the main mystery of the game (Where is Anna?) and the sub plots that the rest of the cast provide, there are no times when you feel like nothing it's happening.
I enjoyed as well the few easter eggs I found,the way each character is written and the decisions, specially the fact that the developers emphasised on the doubt factor, during your gameplay you feel like you are being fooled again and again and that somehow they try to lean you to one side or another even though the right answer it's not clear 100% that "What If..." feeling really made me feel enjoy the development of the outcomes even more.

To make thinks short, buy it. The price compared with the hours of entertainment it gives is in itself a gift.

OK, I have just finished one run and I would recommend it!
In shorts,

Goods:
+Lots of contents, even some random guys on Spark, very detailed characterized even for minor characters
+Climax just bumped into at the right moments
+Innovative gameplay rather than just points and clicks
+Real action characters make the game much more immersive
+There are just right amount of minigames beside pure text reading
+Spot on the mentality that people like to check on others' phones and see what're inside, eg. Gallery, videos, etc
+Low price tag!

Bads:
-I can't say Anna is poor at acting, she's good, but she's kind of zoned out during the first second of most of the clips. It looks like that she is thinking what to say then starts acting after one second
-Some unnecessary jumpscares, the script is good, the story is good, come on, you can make the atmosphere scary without cheap jumpscares, make it more subtle, eg. Anna's wallpaper is changing after certain stages, which is spooky and good
-The ending is not so good... The whole process is great but when it comes to the ending... I am ok with the setting but it would be great if the ending part was made longer
-So during the ending part, Taylor is still busy texting you when he's encountering all those shxx? That doesn't make any sense. I understand that there has to be a means to let the players know what is happening. Can't you just make it like Taylor used Facetime with you before all those happened and try to tell the story with videos? As I imagine the scene, I found it very weird that Taylor is dealing with those things and keeps looking at the phone and texts you back and forth. That would be a heavy smartphone addict...
-The story is too long but very linear, which makes replays not quite possible. I want to try the other endings, but it's harsh for me to go for another 4-hour KNOWN adventure. There are many side events to do but the main route is pretty much the same. Maybe you can make it that we start at some certain late points or make the story less linear. We don't like grinding...

That being said, it's still a very great game, I hope there are more localization subtitles coming soon that I can refer to more of my friends from other parts of the world.

Well, what can I say? Not at all what I expected from this kind of game. I expected to be a little bored. I expected it to feel repetitive. I expected to quit before the game was over. That's not what happened at all. 

The story was engaging to the point of a novel worthy "couldn't put it down" feel. I had to know what was going on and what would happen to the characters involved. Somehow it managed to create an incredible atmosphere that I would not have credited a game that takes place on a mobile phone as being capable of. 

Simulacra kept me guessing till the end. It also has replay value because your choices matter and there is more than one way for this game to end based on the choices you make. 

For the price it can't be faulted and I would have paid more. The best way to play this is on your mobile phone, but I played the first time on my PC and  found it just as immersive. 

This game will not treat you like a child and it will not hold your hand. You will have to think and you will have to figure things out.

I absolutely love both games that come with uncovering lore and mystery as well as characters you can really deeply care for, even if you're mostly contacting them through text.
Simulacra is definitely a story game over a gameplay game -- most of the controls are point and click and most of the "game type" puzzles are rather simple. Simulacra really shines through in its story -- uncovering the overarching mystery behind the disappearance of the phone's original owner, Anna. The game also has replayability with four different endings (Though I've only seen two of them thus far), that change with your actions throughout the game.

Probably my only complaint would be that some of the calls and voice messages can have a bit of hokey acting in them, which can draw you out of the game a bit (Except for Taylor, his actor is pretty awesome).

Overall I'd definitely say it's well worth the price if you're looking for an interesting modern mystery to settle down with, as well as a few spooks now and then.

The first playthrough is the most fun because you get to explore the game's limits and be a catfishing detective, although the replay value is pretty low for me because then you realize just how short it really is. For $5 though, it is acceptable. The buildup is great and the ending is decent and not what I expected, but pretty original in its own way. I also think they did a great job with the interface and laid out relatively natural methods for you to do your investigating. The journey was definitely better than the destination for me.

I am a fan of interactive storytelling, but the only thing you really feel invested in is finding out what happened to Anna, and if you're sympathetic, wanting to save her, since she is the only character you really get to know through all your interactions and discoveries. The biggest con for me is that the acting and voice acting was okay at best - at times a little too animated/forced - and I felt if there were more development for the characters, the attachment would truly tear us apart as we are forced to make more choices. Also, the creep factor disappeared for me personally once I got through to the ending.

Overall, I do recommend the game, but not very enthusiastically. It was good, but has a lot of potential to be even better.

A psychological horror/mystery about invading others privacy and cyberstalking?  Talk about checking all my boxes at once!  I'm in!!!

Okay, so this is a little game about you having someone elses cellphone.  I beat it in a few hours, four maybe, and enjoyed the trip.  Everything you have to do in this game, you do with this cell phone.  You get to break into email accounts, search online registries for sex offenders, and catfish people, all in an attempt to find the ultimate truth.  It's like someone finally based a game off my hobbies.

So, the story is kind of linear, in that you work to unlock new areas of the mystery, piece by piece.  First, you get to play with texts and pictures, then you get enough information to open the email, then you can gather what you need to beat security questions...  I'd say the gameplay is about sifting through information to find what you need to move on.  You also get to talk to the phone owner's friends, and they help to move the plot along, or you can ask them for help if you get stuck.

I say it's linear, but there are actually several branching paths that probably all end up in the same place.  Do you know Telltale games?  Kind of like that...  We might make a different turn here and there, but we're all on the same road with a beginning, middle and end.  Example?  Okay, here's an example...  You need to find out some information from this person through text.  Do you own up, tell them you're a creepo reading through someone elses phone because they might be in trouble, or do you try to bluff your way through, pretending to be who you're not?  Make your choice and either way, life will go on.  I don't think you can get stuck.  Then at the end they have a nice little screen that says things like "You and 68% of players looked at the porn stash," just like a Telltale game.  (there was no porn stash...)

It's pretty creative storywise, and I'm not going to give anything away, but it looked like there were about 4 different endings, and I wouldn't be adverse to trying again sometime to see how things can change.  I only had two of them available to me, so I must have needed to do something else to unlock the others, and I'm not entirely sure what that is, which is good to me.  Means the game still has more meat to it.  It reminded me of another game I played called Her Story, and I didn't recommend that one because one play is all it's good for, but this one was more than double the length and I'd be happy to go again some day.

Scariness, it wasn't scary, but I'm pretty tough to phase.  It likes to make creepy noises in your headphones.  There's some image distortion, but I wouldn't call anything a jump scare, which is good, because those turn people off.

TL:DR I had fun.  Maybe you'll have fun too?  I hope I've given you enough information to know if you'll enjoy it too.  That's why I'm writing all this after all.

Things I like
- Story is gripping, twists are fun although some are quite predictable
- Atmosphere is strong, with the right feelings of paranoia and eerieness.
- Simple controls but with a lot to do
- Character list kept short, but with a lot of personality
- Choices matter

Things I dislike:
- Jumpscares. They're not needed, wanted, or help anything or anyone. They just come up randomly for a cheap shock.
- The endings are either far too vague to properly understand, or too deep to easily understand. I can't tell which, but I didn't get as much from it as I hoped.
- If you accidentally mis-click a dialogue option, or you do something else dumb, there's a good chance you're gonna need to restart the entire game to rectify it. This is also true of endings, so you'd better be prepared to replay the game at least 3 times.
